features.source: The Treaty of Paris: the thirteen states and the land west to the Mississippi.
The Louisiana Purchase, which doubled the country for fifteen million dollars.
Florida, ceded by Spain under the Adams-Onis treaty.
The Oregon Treaty split the joint occupation at the 49th parallel.
Guadalupe Hidalgo ended the war with Mexico, taking the southwest and settling the Texas boundary.
The Gadsden Purchase completed the contiguous border.
The Union alone. Kentucky, Maryland, Delaware, Missouri and the Missouri bootheel stayed in, which is why the frontier runs south of the Ohio in the west.
West Virginia admitted, the only state made out of a seceding one.
The Confederacy's last army surrendered; the seceded states are drawn back in from that day rather than from their individual readmissions.

features.label: Texas (United States)
features.source: Annexed by joint resolution while Mexico still rejected both the annexation and the republic before it — contested ground until Guadalupe Hidalgo.

features.label: Alaska (United States)
features.source: Bought from Russia for 7.2 million dollars.

features.label: Hawaii (United States)
features.source: Annexed by joint resolution five years after the overthrow of the kingdom.

features.label: Puerto Rico (United States)
features.source: Ceded by Spain in the Treaty of Paris.

features.label: Cuba (United States)
features.source: Occupied under military government between Spanish withdrawal and Cuban independence.
